# Development

[繁體中文版 →](DEVELOPMENT.zh-Hant.md)

## The mock exam

The repository holds the app's parts (`web/`) and a small Go program that folds
them into the single file. Building it requires Go ≥ 1.27 and nothing else.

```bash
go test ./...                          # question-bank checks + vet
go run . -export-html dist/mso-ca.html # build the single file
python -m http.server 8321 -d web      # or: serve web/ while developing
```

The bank is `web/questions.json`. Every item has the shape of the real paper: a
stem, four to six numbered statements, which of them are true, and five options
naming sets of them. [`bank/FORMAT.md`](bank/FORMAT.md) records the owner's
decisions about that shape and the rules items are written to; the app shuffles
the statements at every draw and renumbers the options to match.

`go test ./...` is more than a shape check: it guards the faults that quietly
ruin a question bank. Most of the checks were added after a review found the
fault in real questions.

| Check | What it stops |
|---|---|
| Per-module counts; 4 to 6 statements in both languages; five options in display order; exactly one option matching the true statements, and it is the key | items going missing, half-written or mis-keyed |
| Option sets are symmetric: any option the size of the key can be renumbered into it | reading the key off the shape of the option set |
| A note per statement and a trap code per false statement on every item the app reorders | an explanation pointing at the wrong statement once the order changes |
| The number of true statements varies across the bank | learning to hunt for the one false statement |
| No kind of trap dominates | learning to check for one kind of defect only |
| Statement length spread and standout | a false statement given away by being the longest or shortest |
| Statements carrying an absolute or a negation are true at a healthy rate | "mark the absolutes false" |
| Citation has a locator; stems name the topic, never a section number | citing a document with no paragraph to turn to; asking what a number says |
| Statutory Chinese terms | wording the official Chinese editions never use |
| Chinese 該 points back to something already named | "the customer" or "the MSO" rendered word for word as 該客戶 or 該經營者, with nothing before it to refer to |
| Guideline paragraphs are 段 in Chinese | a Guideline paragraph called 款, the Ordinance's word for a subsection |
| ML/TF pairing | dropping the terrorist-financing half in Chinese |
| No false statement turns on "Joint Financial Investigation Unit" | keying false the name C&ED's own sample keys true (register B21) |
| No positional references | "statement 2" or "option B" in a note, when statements and options are reordered |
| No duplicate items, no statement made twice | one point asked twice, or a twin that tells a candidate which to doubt |
| Every statement stores its deciding quote, found word for word in a document the item cites | a statement the cited passage does not decide; a document replaced without its text being extracted again |
| C&ED's own samples carry C&ED's words | "official" on a paraphrase |
| Circulars cited are current | a circular that a later document has overtaken coming back |
| Strategies that read only the option set find the key no more often than chance | the most convergent, most popular, largest or last option pointing at the key |
| A guesser that sees only the statements and options, trained on the bank itself | a new surface tell: it may pick at most 45% of keys (chance 20%) and pass at most 0.5% of simulated papers |
| Each language's fields hold that language only | "the Chinese text says…", or an English abbreviation no Chinese source prints |

The quote check reads `docs/text/`, the extracted text of every document in
`docs/EN` and `docs/TC`, and `docs/quotes.json`, which holds the deciding quotes
per question and language. After adding or replacing a document, run
`python docs/extract_text.py` (it needs PyMuPDF). The check then lists every
quote that the new edition no longer supports.

### Writing items

Before editing sources or questions, read [source maintenance](docs/SOURCE-MAINTENANCE.md).
The reading-order number is the only document ID: `EN 03`, filename prefix 03
and quote `"doc": "03"` all mean the AML/CFT Guideline. Filenames and official
sources are recorded in `docs/catalog.json`. The nine additions are not yet
part of the bank's coverage review. Run `python docs/build_catalog.py --check`
after source metadata or filename changes.

Items are written as patches and checked before they reach the bank, with the
tools in [`bank/`](bank/) (Python 3, standard library only):

```bash
python bank/find.py EN 03 "target market"        # a passage in a source, with page and context
python bank/apply.py next 3 15                   # the next unused ids in module 3
python bank/apply.py check patch.json            # validate a patch
python bank/apply.py apply patch.json            # generate the options, merge into the bank and quotes
python bank/show.py m3-261                       # an item with its key, traps and notes
python bank/blind.py packet patch.json out.md    # the items without their answers, for a blind reviewer
python bank/blind.py compare patch.json ans.json # the reviewer's verdicts against the truth
```

`bank/combo.py` builds every option set from a catalogue of symmetric templates;
nobody writes options by hand.

The method behind that table, and behind the revision pack, is written up as a
reusable skill: see [The skill](#the-skill) below.

Fonts: DM Sans and DM Mono are embedded under the SIL Open Font License; Chinese
text uses the operating system's fonts.

### Historical files

All active items now have per-statement notes and quotes. The temporary
new-format filter, one-off converter and duplicate legacy JSON snapshots
have been removed. That migration and the first repairs reserved 1,511 IDs in
`bank/retired-ids.json`;
`apply.py next` skips them and `apply.py check` rejects their reuse. The final
completion wave reserves 12 further replaced IDs, for 1,523 in total.
The original questions and quotes remain at commit
`7787e991cc7a5c6eb0e22f1c9216ae133f2daf27` (`v1.7.5`):

```bash
git show v1.7.5:web/questions.json
git show v1.7.5:docs/quotes.json
```

The two later replacements, `m3-261` → `m3-322` and `m1-142` → `m1-177`,
preserve their old questions and quotes in [the implementation record](bank/audit/implementation.json).
The audit reports retain their historical baselines and validate the follow-up
against current statements; run `bank/audit/report.py --check`,
`bank/audit/terms_report.py --check`, `bank/audit/p1_report.py --check` and
`bank/audit/remaining_report.py --check` with Python; CI runs all four.
The later P1 additions and their final blind reviews are recorded in
[`bank/audit/p1-implementation.json`](bank/audit/p1-implementation.json),
which verifies the earlier bank without rewriting its audit history.

The [final completion record](bank/audit/remaining-implementation.json) adds the
remaining P2/P3 coverage and preserves each expanded question's retired snapshot.
The validator reconstructs all preceding bank versions, including replacements,
and binds final blind verdicts to their reviewed text. Document 18's image-only form
labels are in `docs/transcripts/18.json`, bound to raw PDF hashes and independently
checked; `docs/extract_text.py` inserts them on their original pages. Recheck the
transcript whenever the PDF changes; the source tests reject stale bindings.

Keep the numbered sources, extracted text, authoring guide and conflicts
register: they are inputs to authoring and verification, not build leftovers.

## The revision pack

The pack is generated from [`revision/`](revision/README.md) with Python 3's
standard library alone:

```bash
python revision/pack_build.py dist/mso-revision-pack.html
```

[`revision/README.md`](revision/README.md) covers its layout, the rules each page
follows, and the review tools.

## The skill

[`.claude/skills/exam-prep/SKILL.md`](.claude/skills/exam-prep/SKILL.md) is the
method behind both files, written for any exam. It covers choosing and checking
the sources, settling conflicts between them, and writing the study pack and the
question bank. It also covers verifying every answer blind, guarding the bank
with tests, and delivering the mock exam. The exam format is a spec the user
defines, so nothing in the skill is tied to this exam; this repository is its
reference implementation.

Its version is in the file's front matter (`metadata.version`). Released skill
versions are tagged `skill-vX.Y.Z` on their source commit. Those tags do not
begin with `v`, so they never trigger a release. Source on `main` may be newer
than the latest publicly released files; public releases require authorization.

| Version | Date | First released in | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.3.0 | 18 Oct 2026 | Source on `main`; see release tags | Adds source-first coverage audits, explicit semantic support checks, image-page and version evidence, scoring-history handling, and scope-aware review costs. Respects settled project decisions and authorization; moves conditional guard/tool detail into references. |
| 2.2.0 | 28 Sep 2026 | v1.7.5 | Adds calibrating a mechanical filter and a cheaper model on a judged sample before a bulk review, with the numbers from this repository's quote sweep. |
| 2.1.0 | 28 Sep 2026 | v1.7.4 | Adds the options-only guesser to the guard catalogue, and what this repository measured once it had the new checks: stored deciding quotes, convergence and echo at chance, and the guesser's results. |
| 2.0.0 | 28 Sep 2026 | v1.7.4 | Renamed `exam-prep`. Covers the study pack and the mock-exam app as well as the bank, and makes the exam format a spec the user defines. ## Releases

Releases are cut by tag. Pushing a tag beginning with `v` runs
[`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml), which vets and tests the bank,
builds the file from that exact commit, and attaches it to a GitHub release
together with the revision pack built from `revision/`. The tests run before the
build, so a tag that fails never becomes a download.

Use an annotated tag: its message becomes the release notes, so say what
changed for a candidate. Keep `--cleanup=whitespace`, or git drops every line
that starts with `#`, Markdown headings included.

```bash

git push origin v1.7.2
```

# 開發說明

## 模擬試

本專案存放程式的組成部分（`web/`）及一個小型 Go 程式，用以把它們合併成單一檔案。產生檔案只需 Go 1.27 或以上，別無其他依賴。

```bash
go test ./...                          # 題庫檢查 + vet
go run . -export-html dist/mso-ca.html # 產生單一檔案
python -m http.server 8321 -d web      # 或：開發時在本機提供 web/
```

題庫為 `web/questions.json`。每道題都採用真實試卷的格式：題幹、4 至 6 句編號陳述、哪幾句正確，以及五個列出陳述組合的選項。[`bank/FORMAT.md`](bank/FORMAT.md) 記錄了題庫擁有人就這個格式所作的決定及出題規則；程式每次抽題都會重新排列陳述，並相應重新編號選項。

`go test ./...` 並非只檢查格式，而是防範一些會悄悄毀掉題庫的問題；大部分檢查都是在審核中真的發現了該問題之後才加入的。

| 檢查項目 | 防範甚麼 |
|---|---|
| 各單元題數；中英文均有 4 至 6 句陳述；五個選項按顯示次序排列；只有一個選項與正確陳述相符，且即為答案 | 題目遺失、只寫了一半或答案標錯 |
| 選項組合須對稱：與答案大小相同的選項，都可經重新編號變成答案 | 從選項組合的結構看出答案 |
| 程式會重新排列陳述的題目，每句陳述均須有講解，每句錯誤陳述均須註明陷阱類別 | 陳述換了次序後，講解指向錯誤的陳述 |
| 正確陳述的數目在題庫內須有變化 | 養成「只找一句錯」的習慣 |
| 陷阱類別不可一面倒 | 只懂得檢查某一種錯處 |
| 陳述長度的分布及突出 | 錯誤陳述因最長或最短而露餡 |
| 含絕對用語或否定詞的陳述須有足夠比例屬正確 | 「見到絕對用語就揀錯」 |
| 出處須有定位；題幹須以文字說明題目，不得引用條文編號 | 只列文件名稱，讀者無從翻查；考背條號 |
| 法定中文用語 | 使用官方中文本從未採用的字眼 |
| 「該」須承接前文已提及的對象 | 把「the customer」或「the MSO」逐字譯成「該客戶」或「該經營者」，前文卻沒有可承接的對象 |
| 《指引》的段落稱「段」 | 把《指引》的段落寫成條例指分條的「款」 |
| ML/TF 對應 | 中文漏掉「恐怖分子資金籌集」那一半 |
| 錯誤陳述不得只錯在 “Joint Financial Investigation Unit” 這個名稱 | 把海關參考試題本身判為正確的寫法判為錯誤（登記冊 B21） |
| 不得以位置稱呼陳述或選項 | 講解寫「陳述2」或「選項B」，但陳述及選項會重新排列 |
| 不得有重複題目，同一陳述不得出現兩次 | 同一點被問兩次，或一對孿生陳述提示考生該懷疑哪一句 |
| 每句陳述均存有決定其對錯的原文，並須在該題所引文件中逐字找到 | 所引段落並不能判定陳述；文件更換後未有重新擷取文字 |
| 海關的參考試題須保留海關原文 | 把改寫的題目標為「官方」 |
| 所引通函均屬現行文件 | 已被較新文件取代的通函再次出現 |
| 只看選項組合的猜題方法，命中率不得高於隨機 | 最趨同、最常見、最大或最後的選項指向答案 |
| 只看陳述及選項、以題庫本身訓練的猜題程式 | 新的表面線索：最多只可猜中 45% 的答案（純粹猜測為 20%），模擬試卷最多只可通過 0.5% |
| 各語言欄位只用該語言 | 「中文本指……」一類說法，或中文來源從未使用的英文縮寫 |

引文檢查會讀取 `docs/text/`（`docs/EN` 及 `docs/TC` 內每份文件擷取的文字）及 `docs/quotes.json`（每題每種語言決定答案的原文）。新增或更換文件後，請執行 `python docs/extract_text.py`（需要 PyMuPDF）；檢查隨即會列出新版文件不再支持的每段引文。

"""Write the text of every document in docs/EN and docs/TC to docs/text/EN|TC/NN.txt.

The question bank's tests check each question's deciding quote against these
files, so run this again whenever a document in docs/ is added or replaced:

    python docs/extract_text.py

Needs PyMuPDF (pip install pymupdf). Pages are separated by a form feed, so the
page of a match is the number of form feeds before it, plus one. CJK
compatibility ideographs, which some of the Chinese PDFs use for common
characters (行 as U+FA08, 金 as U+F90A), are mapped to their unified forms,
and private-use characters, which some PDFs use to draw list bullets, are
dropped. The Ordinance's running footer ("Last updated date … Verified Copy",
最後更新日期 … 經核證文本) is removed from every page, so a passage that runs
across a page break reads as one and a quote can span the break. Nothing else is
changed. Image-only form labels are supplemented from reviewed, page-specific
transcripts in docs/transcripts/NN.json, tied to the PDF's SHA-256. They are
appended to their own page and labelled as transcriptions, not automatic OCR.

The catalog document number is also the filename prefix, quote document number,
extracted-text filename and image-transcript filename.

It also writes docs/text/manifest.json, which records the SHA-256 of the file
each text came from, so the tests can tell when a document has been replaced
without its text being extracted again.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys
import unicodedata

import pymupdf

DOCS = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# The footer the Ordinance prints at the foot of every page, in each language.
FOOTERS = [
    re.compile(r'Last updated date\n\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4}\nAnti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist '
               r'Financing Ordinance\n(?:[^\n]*\n){0,8}?Verified Copy\n'),
    re.compile(r'最後更新日期\n\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4}\n《打擊洗錢及恐怖分子資金籌集條例》\n'
               r'(?:[^\n]*\n){0,8}?經核證文本\n'),
]


def strip_footers(page):
    for footer in FOOTERS:
        page = footer.sub('', page)
    return page


def unify(text):
    out = []
    for c in text:
        if '\ue000' <= c <= '\uf8ff':
            continue  # private-use glyphs: list bullets drawn from a symbol font, not text
        out.append(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', c) if '\uf900' <= c <= '\ufaff' else c)
    return ''.join(out)


def main():
    manifest = {}
    catalog = json.loads((DOCS / 'catalog.json').read_text(encoding='utf8'))
    documents = catalog['documents']
    ids = [document['id'] for document in documents]
    assert ids == [f'{i:02d}' for i in range(1,len(documents)+1)], 'Invalid document order'
    for lang in ('EN', 'TC'):
        out = DOCS / 'text' / lang
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for document in documents:
            num = document['id']
            src = DOCS / lang / document['editions'][lang]['file']
            assert src.name.startswith(num + '_'), src
            if src.suffix == '.pdf':
                with pymupdf.open(src) as pdf:
                    pages = [strip_footers(page.get_text()) for page in pdf]
                transcript = DOCS / 'transcripts' / f'{num}.json'
                if transcript.exists():
                    supplement = json.loads(transcript.read_text(encoding='utf8'))[lang]
                    assert hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == supplement['source_sha256'], \
                        f'Re-check image transcript against changed PDF: {src.name}'
                    for number, lines in supplement['pages'].items():
                        pages[int(number)-1] += '\n[Verified image transcription]\n' + '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
                text = '\f'.join(pages)
            elif src.suffix == '.md':
                text = src.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            else:
                continue
            text = unify(text).replace('\r\n', '\n')
            (out / f'{num}.txt').write_text(text, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
            # Hash with Windows line endings folded, as git may check a text source
            # (the FAQ page) out either way; the tests hash it the same way.
            digest = hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')).hexdigest()
            manifest[f'{lang}/{num}.txt'] = {'source': src.name, 'sha256': digest}
            transcript = DOCS / 'transcripts' / f'{num}.json'
            if src.suffix == '.pdf' and transcript.exists():
                manifest[f'{lang}/{num}.txt']['transcript_sha256'] = hashlib.sha256(
                    transcript.read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')).hexdigest()
            print(f'{lang}/{num}.txt  {len(text):>9,} characters  from {src.name}', file=sys.stderr)
    (DOCS / 'text' / 'manifest.json').write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + '\n', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Maintaining the source documents

[繁體中文版 →](SOURCE-MAINTENANCE.zh-Hant.md)

## One document number

The number in the [reading directory](README.md) is the only document ID.
`catalog.json` lists documents in that order; `id` is the two-digit number.
For example, the AML/CFT Guideline is **03** everywhere:

- Official files: `EN/03_High_…pdf` and `TC/03_高_…pdf`.
- Extracted text: `text/EN/03.txt` and `text/TC/03.txt`.
- Question quotes: `"doc": "03"` in `quotes.json`.
- Image transcripts, where needed: `transcripts/NN.json` with the same number.

Cap. 615 is **04**; the periodic-return circular and its transcript are **18**.
There is no separate stable source ID or old-name lookup.

## Editing or adding material

Use `catalog.json` for filenames, priority, official URLs, editions and hashes.
The original 23 bank sources are marked `original_bank_source`; the nine additions
are reading materials, not evidence that their contents are already covered by
questions. Verify edition, language, applicability and citation patterns in
`sources_test.go` before writing questions against an addition. Item 20 is a
statutory extract; item 22's TC file is an English-source pointer.

After replacing source content, regenerate text with `python docs/extract_text.py`
(requires PyMuPDF) and review affected quotes. Recheck image transcripts against
the new PDF. PDF hashes use raw bytes; Markdown hashes use LF line endings.
Generate the directory with `python docs/build_catalog.py`.

Companion publications live under `related/NN/`, using their parent document's
number. `companions` in the catalog records each publication's language, edition,
URL, raw-file hash and extracted-text hash; `related_documents` links originals
already in the main directory and `online_references` distinguishes live webpages.
Run `python docs/extract_related.py` after changing companion files. These files
are reading supplements, not additional numbered bank sources: do not cite a
companion passage under its parent circular's `doc` value without explicitly
extending the bank's citation checks. Preserve later documentation review evidence
in `bank/audit/maintenance/`; earlier hash records and snapshots stay unchanged.

If reading order changes, renumber filenames, catalog IDs, extracted text,
manifest keys, quotes, transcripts, citation patterns, reports and authoring
examples together. Preserve question IDs, question wording and saved-answer
compatibility. Archive prior audit evidence and record a verified mechanical
migration; a hash change alone is not evidence of a correct migration.

## Checks

```bash
python docs/build_catalog.py --check
go test ./...
python bank/audit/report.py --check
python bank/audit/terms_report.py --check
python bank/audit/p1_report.py --check
python bank/audit/remaining_report.py --check
go run . -export-html dist/mso-ca.html
python revision/pack_build.py dist/mso-revision-pack.html
```

The mock exam stores progress by question ID, not document number. This cleanup
does not change question IDs or stored answers. Historical evidence before the
numbering cleanup is retained in [the audit archive](../bank/audit/history/README.md);
it is not a numbering system to maintain or use for new questions.

[English version →](SOURCE-MAINTENANCE.md)

## 只用一套文件編號

[閱讀目錄](README.zh-Hant.md)的順序就是唯一文件編號。
`catalog.json`按此順序排列，`id`使用兩位數字。例如反洗錢指引在所有地方都是**03**：

- 原件：`EN/03_High_…pdf`及`TC/03_高_…pdf`。
- 擷取文字：`text/EN/03.txt`及`text/TC/03.txt`。
- 題庫引文：`quotes.json`中的`"doc": "03"`。
- 圖片轉錄（如有）：`transcripts/NN.json`也用同一編號。

第615章是**04**；定期申報表通函及其圖片轉錄是**18**。
不再另設固定來源ID，也不再維護舊檔名查找對照。

## 修改或新增資料

檔名、優先級、官方網址、版本及檔案摘要統一記在`catalog.json`。
`original_bank_source`標示既有題庫所用的23份來源；新增9項只是閱讀材料，
不代表已補入題庫。使用新增材料出題前，須核對版本、語言、適用範圍，並在
`sources_test.go`確認引用識別規則。第20項是法例摘錄；第22項的中文檔是英文原文入口。

更換原件內容後，執行`python docs/extract_text.py`（需要PyMuPDF），覆核受影響引文。
有圖片人工轉錄時，須對新PDF重新核對。PDF摘要按原始位元組計算；Markdown先統一為LF換行。
執行`python docs/build_catalog.py`更新雙語閱讀目錄。

通函配套原件放在`related/NN/`，沿用主文件編號。目錄中的`companions`記錄
語言、版本、官方網址、原件及擷取文字摘要；`related_documents`連到庫內已有原件，
`online_references`則明確標示僅在線入口。更改配套原件後執行
`python docs/extract_related.py`。配套資料目前只供閱讀，尚未加入題庫引用核驗；
不能把配套原文當作通函正文，用主文件編號直接出題。後續文件說明的變動證據
追加在`bank/audit/maintenance/`，保留原來的審校摘要及快照。

若調整閱讀順序，須一次同步修改檔名、目錄編號、擷取文字、清單、引文、轉錄、
引用識別規則、報告及教學例子。題號及題目內容保留，避免影響舊作答紀錄。
保留原審校證據並記錄已核驗的機械遷移；不能只改摘要值消除檢查錯誤。

## 檢查

```bash
python docs/build_catalog.py --check
go test ./...
python bank/audit/report.py --check
python bank/audit/terms_report.py --check
python bank/audit/p1_report.py --check
python bank/audit/remaining_report.py --check
go run . -export-html dist/mso-ca.html
python revision/pack_build.py dist/mso-revision-pack.html
```

模擬試按題號保存進度，不按文件編號保存。此次清理沒有改題號或作答內容。
統一編號前的原始審校證據保存在[歷史存檔](../bank/audit/history/README.md)，
只供追溯，不作為往後出題或維護的另一套編號。

# Authoring guide for the MSO revision pack Paths below are relative to `revision/`. See `README.md` for building and checking. ## What the pack is A bilingual (English / Traditional Chinese) single-file HTML revision pack for the Hong Kong C&ED **Money Service Operator (MSO) Competence Assessment**: 35 multiple-choice questions, seven modules of five ((1) general AML/CFT and counter proliferation financing knowledge; (2) AMLO Parts 1–7; (3) AMLO Schedules; (4) C&ED guidelines; (5) systems and controls: institutional governance and strategy; (6) AML/CFT control areas; (7) demonstrating and monitoring compliance). Pass = no more than 2 wrong in any module AND ≥25/35. The reader is an MSO owner memorising for a closed-book exam. They read in three modes: English only, Chinese only, or both. Pages are generated by Python modules in this folder (one module per page, plus figure modules) and assembled by `pack_build.py`. Look at `gl.py` + `gl_fig.py` (the Guidelines page) and `s2x.py` as models. `review/extract.py` writes the current text of every page, section by section, to `review/sections/*.txt` (EN VIEW and TC VIEW). Grep those before writing so you never repeat what another page already says — link to it instead (`Schedule 2 page`). ## The reader's rules (from the owner's own feedback — follow them exactly) - **Situation first.** Headings and card titles state the situation or the plain rule. Never make a section or paragraph number the subject of a heading ("¶7.13 says…" is wrong; "Staff reports go straight to the MLRO, unfiltered" is right). Citations trail as support. - **Format hierarchy:** a process or interaction → a **flowchart**; rules that change with the situation → a **table whose rows are the scenarios**; key numbers and deadlines → a **number table** (`numreq`: the number | what it requires | when it applies | if it is missed); **bullet points only as a last resort** (the checker flags `
  • `). Every page should visualise its key content (at least one figure per page, more where there is a process). - **Highlight what is easy to confuse** with `trap(...)` callouts ("Easy to confuse") and `flag()` markers inside table cells. Prefer `vs=[...]` side-by-side contrasts. - **Colour must carry a stated meaning and be keyed.** Every figure that uses node colours gets a `legend([...])` passed to `fig(...)`. Kinds: `must` (red: a duty/deadline/consequence for you), `may` (amber: a power or discretion someone else holds), `ok` (green: a safe outcome/protection), `stop` (black: an end state such as refusal, offence), `faint` (dashed: background/context), `''` (plain grey: a neutral step), `hex` (a question node, `Node(..., shape='hex')`). - **No section-by-section listings, no "who is who" filler, no drill/quiz sections, no standalone "numbers" section** — numbers live in the section they arise in. - **Don't repeat the page overview** in the paragraph above the first diagram; that paragraph says how to read the diagram. - **Chinese view contains only Chinese; English view only English.** Bilingual appears only in the combined view. Every text is an (en, tc) pair. - **Each language view follows its own source text.** Where the English and Chinese texts of a document differ (may / 將, or / 及, should / 必須), the English view says what the English text says and the Chinese view what the Chinese text says. Never compare the two versions on the page. A point that exists in one language's text only can be shown in that view only, with the `only-en` / `only-tc` classes. The exceptions are the items the owner decided as one answer for both views (`CONFLICT-CALLS.md`): there the view whose own passage departs teaches the decision from passages in its own language that support it, and may show the departing wording as easy to confuse, in that view only. ## Accuracy — the non-negotiable part Every sentence must be grounded in a source passage, and every table cell, card and callout carries a citation to the paragraph/section that supports it. The pack uses the original 23 sources; the archive has 32 reading materials. Use the reading-order number as the only document ID in filenames, extracted text and quotes. For example, 03 is the AML/CFT Guideline and 04 is Cap. 615. Resolve filenames through `../docs/catalog.json` and read [source maintenance](../docs/SOURCE-MAINTENANCE.md) before using additions or replacing sources. - Paraphrase faithfully; keep conditions, qualifiers and modal strength (must / should / may). - Never invent examples, numbers or lists and present them as the source's. If you illustrate, say so. - Chinese must use the **official Chinese terms of the Chinese source** it cites (`../docs/text/TC/03.txt`, `../docs/text/TC/04.txt`): e.g. 可疑交易報告, 聯合財富情報組 (short form 財富情報組), 洗錢報告主任, 合規主任, 通風報訊, 客戶盡職審查, 更嚴格的客戶盡職審查措施, 政治人物, 實益擁有人, 風險為本的方法, 機構層面的洗錢／恐怖分子資金籌集風險評估 (the Guideline's only form; 機構層面的風險評估 is the FAQ's), 針對性金融制裁, 擴散資金籌集, 指定各方 / 被指認各方 (as the paragraph says), 恐怖分子財產, 批給, 會面, 應考能力評核, 數據庫, 複本, 證明人, 覆核, 職員, 打擊洗錢／恐怖分子資金籌集制度. Check each term in the source before use. - The documents do not share one vocabulary: take the word from the document a cell cites (the Licensing Guide says 業務處所 and 銀行帳戶, the Business Plan guideline 營業處所 and 銀行戶口; Schedule 2 writes 虛擬資產轉賬, the Guideline 虛擬資產轉帳). Some text extracts store common characters as look-alike code points (行 as U+FA08, 金 as U+F90A), so normalise them before concluding that a term is absent. - Short names are labels, not key terms: AMLO and 《打擊洗錢條例》, and the abbreviations MSO and CDD, which the official sample paper itself uses, may appear anywhere, including beside a passage that cites only the Ordinance (which calls itself "this Ordinance" / 本條例). The owner decided this on 27 September 2026. - If two documents conflict, teach the side the owner chose (`CONFLICT-CALLS.md`); for a conflict not listed there, say so neutrally and ask the owner rather than picking one silently. ## Citations - AML/CFT Guideline paragraph: `"¶7.13"` (auto-converted to 第7.13段 in Chinese). Several: `"¶7.13–7.14"`, `"¶2.4(d)"`. Chapter: `"Ch. 7"`. - AMLO section: `"s.25A"`; Schedule 2 section: `"s.13 Sch. 2"`. Other ordinances need an explicit pair: `("DTROP s.25A(1)", "《販毒（追討得益）條例》第25A(1)條")`, `("OSCO s.25", "《有組織及嚴重罪行條例》第25條")`, `("UNATMO s.12", "《聯合國（反恐怖主義措施）條例》第12條")`, `("UNSO", "《聯合國制裁條例》")`, `("WMD(CPS)O s.4", "《大規模毀滅武器（提供服務的管制）條例》第4條")` — take the exact names from document 03 (`../docs/text/TC/03.txt`). - Join several with `cc(a, b)` (define it as in gl.py) or write `"¶7.13 · s.25A"`. - Tuple citations `(en, tc)` must contain no Latin words in the Chinese half. ## API (import with `from ui import *`; see ui.py and bl_core.py) - `sec(id, margin_list, (h2_en, h2_tc), body_html)` — one section. `margin_list` items are citation strings or (en, tc) pairs (short). Section ids must be unique within your page; they become `-`. - `P(en, tc)` paragraph; `h3(en, tc)`; `B(en, tc)` inline pair; HTML inside strings is allowed (``, links). Escape `&` as `&` in HTML text (not inside citations or figure text). - `table([th(en,tc), ...], [tr(rh(en,tc,cite), td(en,tc,cite, post=flag()), ...), ...], note=..., minw=720, cls='')` — `cls='cmp'` gives fixed equal columns for side-by-side comparisons. `td(..., cls='pen')` blurs in recall mode (use for penalties/numbers). - `numreq([ ((num_en,num_tc), (req_en,req_tc), (when_en,when_tc), (miss_en,miss_tc), cite), ... ], heading=True)` - `trap((title_en,title_tc), (body_en,body_tc) or None, cite, vs=[((lab_en,lab_tc),(txt_en,txt_tc)), ...])`, wrapped in `traps(trap(...), trap(...))`. - `chip(en, tc, 'ink')`, `YES`, `NO` for verdict cells (`f'{YES}'`). - Figures: write `def fig_x():` returning `svg(W, H, body, (aria_en, aria_tc), 'uniqueMarkerId', minw)` and place it with `fig(fig_x, (caption_en, caption_tc), legend([...]))` — **pass the function, not its result**: the pack draws each figure three times, once laid out per language view. Building blocks: `Card(x, w, (title_en,title_tc), (body_en,body_tc) or None, kind, cite, href=None, minh=0, answer=False)` (bold title + body; preferred), `Node(x, w, (en,tc), cite, kind, shape='hex')` (a question), `place([([n1, n2], gap_after), ([n3], gap), ...], y0=14)` sets y and returns height; `edge([p1, p2, ...], (lab_en,lab_tc), lx, ly, anchor, mid='uniqueMarkerId')` with points like `n.bottom`, `n.top`, `n.left`, `n.right`, `(x, y)`; `mlabel(x, y, en, tc)` for an edge label; `lines_down(cx, y_top, [en lines], [tc lines], 'c-sans', size)` from `bl_figs` for free text. Use a marker id unique in the whole pack (prefix it with your page key, e.g. 'g7a'). Figures are ~1000 units wide (min-width 860) and display ~870px wide. Sizes you pass are multiplied by FS=1.25 automatically; keep the defaults (Card 11.5/12.5, Node 12) or larger — never smaller than 10.5. Keep connectors from crossing text or boxes; put yes/no labels right beside their branch; give every arrow an obvious start and end; do not reuse the same x for unrelated arrows. - Box text wraps by itself and never splits a Chinese term listed in `bl_core.PROTECT`. If a figure splits another term, add it to that list; `pack_build.py` reports any listed term it finds split across lines. - `answer=True` on outcome boxes lets recall mode blur them. ## Module contract Write `.py` (and optionally `_fig.py`). It must define: - `_BODY` — the concatenated sections (string), `_NAV` — `[(section_id, en_label, tc_label), ...]` in page order (labels 1–4 words), and - `_META = dict(tab=("1","1"), short=(en, tc), eyebrow=(en, tc), title=(en, tc), lede=(en, tc), foot=(en, tc))` — `short` is the outline heading (e.g. ("Guideline Ch. 7 · STR", "指引第7章 · 可疑交易報告")); `eyebrow` like ("AML/CFT Guideline · Chapter 7 · Module 6", "《打擊洗錢指引》第7章 · 單元六"); `title` a short name; `lede` 2–4 sentences on what the chapter decides for the reader (not a list of sections); `foot` names the exact sources drawn on. No `&` in `short`/`tab`. ## Check your work (mandatory loop) Build the pack first (`python pack_build.py`), then run, from `revision/`: `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python review/page_check.py _BODY _NAV ` It prints problems (language purity, dead links, figures not drawn per view, bullets, duplicate ids) and renders every figure to `review/preview/_figN_{en,tc,both}.png`. Open every PNG and look hard: overlapping or clipped text, labels far from lines, arrows crossing boxes/text, cramped or half-empty boxes, small text. Fix and re-run until the checker is clean and the figures look right. Also re-read your text against the sources once more at the end.

"""Keep audit baselines verifiable after reviewed additions and replacements."""
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256((ROOT / path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def check_hash(path, expected):
    data = (ROOT / path).read_bytes()
    variants = [data]
    if pathlib.Path(path).suffix.lower() in {'.json', '.md', '.py', '.txt', '.go'}:
        # Git uses LF in the index and may check text out as CRLF on Windows.
        # Permit only this byte-level conversion, never a content change.
        lf = data.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
        variants.extend([lf, lf.replace(b'\n', b'\r\n')])
    assert any(hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest() == expected for value in variants), f'Snapshot changed: {path}'

def encoded(value, newline):
    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + '\n').replace('\n', newline).encode('utf8')

def validate_reviews(record, current):
    reviewed = set()
    for review in record['blind_review']['items']:
        a = review['answer']; q = current[a['id']]; reviewed.add(q['id'])
        text = {'id':q['id'], 'module':q['module'], 'source':q['source'],
                **{l:{k:q[l][k] for k in ['q','statements']} for l in ['en','tc']}}
        actual = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        assert actual == review['reviewed_text_sha256'], q['id']
        expected = ['T' if t else 'F' for t in q['truth']]
        assert a['verdicts'] == a['tc_verdicts'] == expected, q['id']
    assert reviewed == set(record['added_question_ids']), 'Every addition needs a final bilingual blind review'

    if (path, expected) in state.get('historical_versions', set()):
        return  # Reconstructed preceding wave or preserved documentation text.
